title: Kochi cloudburst, 28 May 2024
what_happened: A short, intense downpour the IMD later confirmed as a cloudburst over Kalamassery flooded parts of Kochi during the morning of 28 May 2024. Rain water entered over 200 houses near Kalamassery and a city IT park, markets and several low-lying neighbourhoods were waterlogged.

rainfall.basis: IMD automatic weather station at CUSAT's Thrikkakara campus recorded ~103 mm in one hour (09:30-10:30); a station ~1 km away logged 100 mm in the same hour; CUSAT researchers cited 98.4 mm in 90 minutes. 100 mm in 1 h is the round figure used here.

scoring.note: The ground truth is news reports naming neighbourhoods, so its spatial precision is about a neighbourhood, not a street. Each locality is an approximate centroid; the tolerance absorbs that. The test asks whether the places reporting flooding fall among the worst spots the screening flags, more often than a point placed at random in the same area would.

localities.name: Kalamassery
localities.report: Cloudburst epicentre; rain water entered over 200 houses.
localities.note: This is where the rain fell hardest, so a flag here is the least independent of the three.

localities.name: Edappally
localities.report: Houses inundated in low-lying areas under Kochi Corporation.

localities.name: Kakkanad (Infopark)
localities.report: Severe waterlogging at Infopark and the surrounding tech hub.

localities.name: Thammanam
localities.report: Houses inundated in low-lying areas under Kochi Corporation.

localities.name: Palarivattom
localities.report: Named only for traffic snarl-ups, not for standing water. Held out of the scoring as a weak case rather than counted as a positive.
